Rafael / Marissa —

Quick legal input and three redline options attached (MSA_term_redlines.docx). Top-line guidance below so you can pick a preferred approach to present to Acme: 

Option A (default, lowest commercial friction):
- Auto-renew: 12-month renewal terms; either party may elect not to renew by providing written notice at least 60 days before the then-current term expiration.
- TFC: Mutual termination for convenience permitted with 60 days' notice; Redwood will provide transition assistance and refund unused prepaid Hosted credits on a pro rata basis. No termination fee for Hosted services.

Option B (protect Dedicated economics):
- Same auto-renew language as A.
- For Dedicated (reserved capacity) services: TFC permitted only with either (i) 90 days' notice or (ii) a buyout equal to the remaining committed fees for the unexpired portion of the term. This preserves reserved hardware economics.

Option C (narrow TFC scope):
- TFC allowed for non-reserved/hosted services only; Dedicated capacity requires termination per the Order Form and early termination fees apply.

Other notes: 
- Data handback/runout: 60 days of transition assistance is fine; suggest we add explicit migration assistance obligations and a security checklist for handback.
- Auto-renew grace timing: add a short confirmation flow (we send renewal reminder 75 days before term end, Acme must notify within 60 days).

I'll attach the redline and a short comment summary. If you agree to Option A + Dedicated carve as in Option B (i.e., mutual TFC but Dedicated requires buyout or 90-day notice), that is my recommended compromise.

Attachment: MSA_term_redlines.docx
